run_text:
Scope: the SAIPEN behaviours this tree actually exercised in one session — the T-1331 lifecycle (SCOUT/BUILD/VERIFY/REVIEW/SHIP/DONE), the branch move off a 352-file dirty tree, the conformance remediation that produced 47 reverify receipts, and the improve cycle lifecycle. Partial context by construction: no other seat's history was read.

IMP-001 [P2] [OTHER] [observed] [ticket]
expected: a blocking conformance finding that is itself a stale improve DRAFT is either classified or names its executable route, so an operator is never left holding a red gate whose remediation list points only at unrelated tickets.
actual: the 17:47:23 core FAIL receipt carried an unclassified improve-report finding for cycle imp-vacterro-fastprompter-20260927-1 — a DRAFT report bound to the pre-move head d80ea43 whose protocol_fingerprint no longer matched the install — but its remediation_commands named only the two reverify tickets. The route that actually cleared it had to be derived by hand (`saipen improve abort <cycle>`), and until that guess every continuation was blocked.
evidence: .saipen/recovery/conformance/2026-09-27T17_47_23.075885Z_receipt-fa5932999cec_core_FAIL.json — blocking_findings.problems[2] is rule_id=unclassified and names the report fingerprint; the same receipt's remediation_commands are ['saipen work reverify T-1231', 'saipen work reverify T-1240'] and its canonical_next_command is the reverify of T-1231. `saipen improve status` at that moment reported `buffy-01: INVALID_REPORT (report_status draft)` and named no route.

IMP-002 [P1] [LOGIC_ERROR] [reproduced] [ticket]
expected: the canonical `work reverify` remediation for a ticket whose contract is the project's own strict gate runs to completion and records the real exit code.
actual: the engine's default command timeout is shorter than this project's strict gate (pytest tests/ takes 604 s wall), so the identical command records an honest FAIL with exit_code null and timed_out true unless the operator happens to pass a longer --timeout. Neither the refusal text nor the gate's remediation string mentions --timeout, so the prescribed single command can never succeed as printed.
evidence: .saipen/recovery/conformance/reverify/RV-000377.json — work T-1240, verdict FAIL, verification[0] command `python -m pytest tests/ -q`, duration_ms 581642, exit_code null, timed_out true. .saipen/recovery/conformance/reverify/RV-000379.json — work T-1240, verdict PASS_WITH_CARRIED_DEBT, byte-identical command, exit_code 0, timed_out absent. The only difference between the two invocations was `--timeout 900`. Red control: the same gate was reverified this way for T-1231 (RV-000378 PASS, exit_code 0) and for 44 further tickets with sub-40-second contracts, so the failure tracks the command duration, not the ticket.

IMP-003 [P2] [OTHER] [observed] [ticket]
expected: `continue` re-evaluates the conformance gate against the receipts currently on disk rather than replaying a verdict computed before the remediation landed.
actual: T-1240's PASS receipt was written at 18:34:41Z, yet `continue --json` kept returning CONFORMANCE_UNHEALTHY, still naming T-1240, and kept serving the 18:25:09Z core FAIL receipt written before that receipt existed. Only an explicit `saipen validate` computed a fresh verdict (18:41:58Z, 0 problems); continuation then routed normally to the improve cycle. An operator who trusts the gate message the launcher prints is told a false blocker for as long as no explicit validate runs.
evidence: .saipen/recovery/conformance/2026-09-27T18_25_09.026736Z_receipt-e95ceb87912b_core_FAIL.json (blocking T-1240) has a timestamp 9 minutes older than .saipen/recovery/conformance/reverify/RV-000379.json (created_at 2026-09-27T18:34:41Z, PASS_WITH_CARRIED_DEBT, same source_head 38c45b8f and same source_tree_fingerprint as the FAIL receipt); .saipen/recovery/conformance/2026-09-27T18_41_58.478950Z_receipt-bcd0d15fad4e_core_PASS.json was written by `saipen validate` and reports verdict PASS with problem_count 0, after which `continue --json` returned IMPROVE_AUDIT_ASSIGNMENT.
